title: Rotate-then-scale non-uniformly shears a mesh (the diamond cart)
summary: A 4-sided CylinderGeometry turned by pi/4 and then scaled non-uniformly comes out as a sheared diamond: an Object3D's matrix applies scale before rotation. Build the shape as its own geometry.

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

usage.example: new THREE.Mesh(frustum(1.5, .95, 1.15, .65, .6), mat)   // module.any.frustum; or bake: geometry.rotateY(Math.PI / 4) THEN mesh.scale

doc.when: Any tapered box or rotated primitive that also needs non-uniform scale.
doc.avoid: mesh.rotation + mesh.scale with different x/z on a rotated primitive.
gotchas: geometry.rotateY() bakes the rotation into the vertices, so a later mesh.scale is applied in the rotated frame correctly.

problem.symptom: A box-like tub renders as a diamond/parallelogram.
problem.cause: Mesh matrix = T * R * S: the non-uniform scale acts on the unrotated axes, then the rotation shears the result.
problem.fix: Build the geometry directly (frustum) or bake the rotation into the geometry before scaling.
problem.detect: Corners not at right angles from above.
